course_name_original: TECNOLOGIE E SISTEMI WEB Canale unico
course_name_en: WEB TECHNOLOGIES AND SYSTEMS Single channel
prerequisites: Knowledge of at least one high-level programming language.
Possibly, knowledge of a query language for relational databases (SQL).

learning_outcomes.text: Know HTML and XML, the standard languages for representing information on the Web. Know the standards, methods, and tools for processing these languages: style sheets for HTML (CSS), DOM HTML, libraries and tools for HTML (Bootstrap), XML stylesheets.
Know client-side Web programming (Javascript, JSON, JQuery).
Know some elements of server-side Web programming (PHP, Node.js).
The main standards for representing and processing information on the World Wide Web. Techniques for client-side programming of Web applications.
Be able to design the client-side of a Web application.
Be able to evaluate the quality of a Web application, with particular regard to the client-side of the application.

The course's project activities and exercises enable the student to communicate/share the requirements of a Web application, as well as the design choices and methodologies for designing and developing the client-side of such an application.

In addition to the classic learning abilities provided by the theoretical study of didactic material, the course delivery methods, particularly the project activities, stimulate students to autonomously deepen certain topics presented in the course, to work in groups, and to concretely apply the notions and techniques learned during the course.
Know the fundamental principles of the World Wide Web and the HTTP protocol: describe the Web architecture, the role of client and server, and the main HTTP methods and status codes.
Know markup languages and HTML5 specifications: recognize and apply the semantic constructs of HTML5 to structure accessible and semantically correct pages.
Design and implement complete and validatable HTML forms: know how to build forms with appropriate fields and client-side and server-side validation mechanisms.
Design responsive layouts with CSS: use style sheets, selectors, box model, flexbox/grid, and media queries to create adaptive interfaces on mobile and desktop devices.
Understand and manipulate the Document Object Model (DOM): navigate and modify the structure of a page using DOM APIs, updating content, attributes, and style in response to events.
Program client interactions with JavaScript: write JavaScript code for event handling, dynamic validation, code modularity, and proper use of callbacks/Promises/async-await.
Use JavaScript libraries and frameworks (e.g., jQuery) and AJAX techniques: integrate a library to simplify DOM manipulations and use AJAX/fetch for asynchronous communication with the server.
Develop server-side components with PHP or Node.js: implement endpoints, handle HTTP requests, sessions and form submissions, and understand basic security concepts (e.g., input sanitization).
Know XML and related technologies (DOM XML, XPath, XSLT): read and transform XML documents using XPath and XSLT for integration and presentation purposes.
Design and implement a complete client-server flow: integrate front-end (HTML/CSS/JS) and back-end (PHP/Node.js) to create functional, testable, and maintainable Web applications.

assessment_methods.method: Written exam with exercises and questions
Practical project (optional, in groups of two or three people)

assessment_rules: To pass the exam, a minimum score of 18/30 is required. The student must demonstrate sufficient knowledge of all program topics and be able to apply acquired notions in the development of an entire web application (if a practical project is chosen) or specific parts (if a written exam is chosen). To achieve 30/30 cum laude, the student must demonstrate excellent knowledge of all topics, connecting them logically and coherently.
